title: The Subscription Kraken
caption:
Check your subscriptions this week. Many people pay for services they forgot they had, and a monthly fee adds up to a year of cost. List them, cancel what you do not use. Educational content, not financial advice.

prompt: Hyper-realistic, photorealistic 10-second vertical 9:16 comedy sequence in one continuous shot, fast kinetic handheld camera, no cuts. ONE human character only, no other people. Character: a stressed man in his thirties, round tired face, messy short brown hair, dark circles under his eyes, wearing a rumpled grey hoodie and pajama bottoms with small cartoon toast on them, holding a coffee mug that says nothing, fully awake in panic. Setting: a cramped morning kitchen, pale daylight from one window, a toaster on the counter. Gag: a gigantic green kraken made of glowing credit-card shaped tentacles bursts out of the open toaster and out of the kitchen cabinets, each tentacle tip holding a tiny glowing monthly payment slip, tentacles wrapping the kettle, the fridge door and his ankles while the toaster pings. Timing: 0 to 2 seconds, he stands calmly sipping coffee as the toaster lever clicks down, the camera pushes in on his face. At 2 seconds the kraken explodes out of the toaster with a wet roar, tentacles whipping across the kitchen, the camera whip-pans to follow one tentacle. At 3 seconds he snaps into a snap-zoom close-up, eyes huge, coffee dripping, and he screams the line at the lens in a hoarse panicked comic voice, American accent, clear: Check your subscriptions this week. His lips move exactly with these five words and nothing else is spoken. At the word subscriptions a tentacle slaps him across the face with a payment slip stuck to his forehead. At the word week the kraken freezes, tentacles go limp, and the toaster pops up a single burnt slice that reads nothing. From 6 to 10 seconds a fast pull-back reveals the whole wrecked kitchen, the kraken gently retreating into the toaster like a shy cat, while he stands covered in slime holding the slice like a trophy, deadpan. Style: absurd photoreal comedy, bright natural light with sticky green slime sheen, shallow depth of field, anamorphic flare, fine 35mm grain, 24fps. Audio: his voice, a wet roar, toaster ping, slapping tentacles, no music. Strict rules: ONE human only, same face, hoodie and pajamas in every frame, mouth clearly articulating, no subtitles, no readable text or numbers anywhere, no logos, no morphing of his face.

title: The Cat Landlord
line: Pay yourself first, then pay the landlord.
caption:
Pay yourself first, then pay the landlord. Setting aside savings the moment you are paid, before bills, is one of the oldest money habits. Even a small amount counts. Educational content, not financial advice.

prompt: Hyper-realistic, photorealistic 10-second vertical 9:16 comedy sequence in one continuous shot, fast kinetic handheld camera, no cuts. ONE human character only, no other people. Character: a young woman about twenty-six, oval face, long wavy black hair tied in a messy bun, tired eyebrows, wearing an oversized mustard cardigan over a white tee, one sock missing, sitting on the floor of a nearly empty apartment holding a small piggy bank in both arms like a baby. Setting: a bare studio apartment at dusk, moving boxes, one lamp. Gag: a huge fluffy orange cat in a tiny black top hat and a gold monocle, standing upright on two legs like a stern landlord, holds a clipboard and taps one paw on a stack of envelopes, a second tiny gold-collared cat butler stands behind him with a stopwatch. Timing: 0 to 2 seconds, she clutches the piggy bank, the orange cat landlord slams the door open and marches in, camera whip-pans to him. At 2 seconds a fast snap-zoom onto her face, she looks straight into the lens, takes a deep breath, and says in a calm, smug, funny deadpan female voice, clear: Pay yourself first, then pay the landlord. Her lips move exactly with these eight words and nothing else is spoken. At the words pay yourself first she kisses the piggy bank loudly and it gives a golden ding. At the word landlord the cat landlord raises one paw to speak and the cat butler pushes the stopwatch which explodes into a burst of confetti. From 6 to 10 seconds a rapid orbit around the two as the cat landlord sighs dramatically, drops a single coin into her piggy bank, bows, and walks out through a cat-sized door, while she gives the lens a tiny victorious smile. Style: absurd photoreal comedy, warm dusk lamp light, shallow depth of field, anamorphic flare, fine 35mm grain, 24fps. Audio: her voice, the dramatic sigh of the cat, the piggy-bank ding, confetti pop, no music. Strict rules: ONE human only, same face, cardigan and hair in every frame, the cats are realistic animals, mouth clearly articulating, no subtitles, no readable text or numbers anywhere, no logos, no morphing.

title: The Emergency Fund Cannon
line: Build a small emergency fund before you invest.
caption:
Build a small emergency fund before you invest. Many planners suggest starting with a cushion for surprise bills, so a flat tire does not force you to sell investments at a bad time. Educational content, not financial advice.

prompt: Hyper-realistic, photorealistic 10-second vertical 9:16 comedy sequence in one continuous shot, fast kinetic handheld camera, no cuts. ONE human character only, no other people. Character: a stocky cheerful man in his forties, broad friendly face, thick black mustache, bald head, wearing a bright orange hard hat, a yellow high-visibility vest over a white shirt and brown work trousers. Setting: a rain-soaked suburban street at night under one flickering streetlamp, a bright red cartoonishly oversized circus cannon sits on the wet asphalt beside his battered tiny yellow car with a flat front tire. Gag: he stands proudly next to the cannon holding a tall glass jar of golden coins labeled with no text, a huge arriving storm cloud rolls in overhead, lightning flickers, and a flood of rainwater rushes down the street. Timing: 0 to 2 seconds, he shakes the coin jar triumphantly at the lens, camera low and whipping around him as thunder rumbles. At 2 seconds a fast snap-zoom onto his face, he locks onto the lens and says in a warm, booming, slightly ridiculous announcer voice, clear: Build a small emergency fund before you invest. His lips move exactly with these nine words and nothing else is spoken. At the words small emergency fund he pours the coins into the cannon. At the word invest he lights the fuse, the cannon blasts out a spray of coins that rises over the street and every coin lands neatly onto the flat tire, which inflates instantly with a comic whoosh. From 6 to 10 seconds a rapid crane-up and pull-back as the flood passes harmlessly under his lifted car and he throws his arms up in victory, rain turning golden in the streetlamp light. Style: absurd photoreal comedy, wet neon street, volumetric rain, anamorphic flare, fine 35mm grain, 24fps. Audio: his voice, thunder, the cannon boom, coins rattling, tire whoosh, no music. Strict rules: ONE human only, same face, mustache, hard hat and vest in every frame, mouth clearly articulating, no subtitles, no readable text or numbers anywhere, no logos, no morphing.
